tips.title: Financial Tips
tips.subtitle: Short guides to organize your money — no data required, just good habits.

ten-tips.title: 10 Tips for Financial Organization
ten-tips.description: Small habits that keep your money under control, one day at a time.

track-expenses.title: Write down every expense
track-expenses.body: Record everything you spend, cash or card. What isn't tracked can't be controlled.

goals.title: Set realistic goals
goals.body: Give your money a direction: short-, medium-, and long-term targets keep you focused.

budget.title: Build a monthly budget
budget.body: Plan where your income goes before the month starts, then follow the plan.

pay-yourself-first.title: Pay yourself first
pay-yourself-first.body: Set your savings aside the day the money arrives — spend what's left, not the other way around.

cut-expenses.title: Cut unnecessary expenses
cut-expenses.body: Subscriptions and small daily habits add up fast; cancel what you don't really use.

impulse.title: Avoid impulse purchases
impulse.body: Wait before buying anything non-essential — the urge usually fades.

installments.title: Avoid installments
installments.body: Splitting a purchase hides its true cost and promises future income you haven't earned yet.

emergency-fund.title: Build an emergency fund
emergency-fund.body: Aim for three to six months of expenses so a surprise doesn't become a debt.

review.title: Review your money regularly
review.body: Check your budget every week and adjust before small leaks grow.

tool.title: Use a tracking tool
tool.body: An app that logs income and expenses keeps the whole picture in one place.

save-money.title: How to Save Money
save-money.description: A straightforward path from deciding to save to watching the balance grow.

goal.title: Set a clear goal
goal.body: Know what you are saving for and by when — a goal without a date is just a wish.

numbers.title: Know your numbers
numbers.body: Add up your income and every expense to see how much you can actually set aside.

cut.title: Cut the superfluous
cut.body: Small daily savings compound into the bulk of what you'll accumulate.

save-first.title: Save first, spend later
save-first.body: Move the money to savings on payday, before any spending.

automate.title: Automate the transfer
automate.body: A scheduled transfer keeps the promise to yourself even on busy months.

extra-income.title: Look for extra income
extra-income.body: Sell what you no longer use or add a side gig to speed things up.

progress.title: Track your progress
progress.body: Watch the balance grow against the goal and celebrate each milestone.

six-jars.title: The Six Jars Method
six-jars.description: Split every income into six fixed shares so every area of life gets funded.

necessities.title: Necessities
necessities.body: Housing, food, transport, and bills — the fixed cost of living.

freedom.title: Financial freedom
freedom.body: Invest so your money eventually works for you.

education.title: Education
education.body: Courses, books, and skills that raise your earning power.

savings.title: Savings and goals
savings.body: The long-term projects — a trip, a car, a house.

fun.title: Fun
fun.body: Guilt-free spending — enjoy the money you worked for.

giving.title: Giving
giving.body: Donate to causes and people you believe in.

organize-strategy.title: A Strategy to Organize Your Finances
organize-strategy.description: Six steps to take your finances from chaos to a working plan.

map.title: Map income and expenses
map.body: List everything coming in and going out for a full month — knowledge comes first.

debts.title: Organize your debts
debts.body: List what you owe, prioritize the most expensive, and negotiate what you can.

cut.title: Cut superfluous spending
cut.body: With the map in hand, trim what doesn't serve your goals.

reserve.title: Build an emergency reserve
reserve.body: Protect the plan: savings for the unexpected come before investments.

goals.title: Set goals and plan
goals.body: Turn intention into numbers: a target, a date, and a monthly amount.

monitor.title: Monitor and adjust
monitor.body: Review monthly — a budget is a living plan, not a one-time document.

cdi.title: CDI example: a share of the DI rate

financial-independence.subtitle: How much to put away every month to reach a target — and how much an accumulated balance pays out monthly.

accumulation.title: Reaching a target
accumulation.description: The monthly contribution that turns today's balance into your target over the years, net of inflation, fees, and income tax on the gains.

withdrawal.title: Living off the accumulation
withdrawal.description: The constant monthly withdrawal an accumulated balance supports over the years — the tax charged on the interest share only.

general.title: General
general.description: The time zone decides what "today" is for recurring transactions and new entries. The main currency is what limits and goals are counted in, and the default for new accounts. Changing the zone never shifts what is recorded; changing the currency never converts amounts.
